memo.verdict: Neutral; park with a price trigger; medium conviction. Hexpol (HPOL.B-SE) at SEK 97.05 (2026-10-06) is "the right story at the wrong price, by about 12 percent": a change-of-regime case at a good, slow business with a cyclical turn arriving at the same time, where the modal return of 13.9 percent a year over eighteen months and 12.7 percent a year over three years is a C against the 20 percent bar. The park rule does not bite (management C, business quality B, transmission C, trackability C; no D or F on a gate attribute); the park is on price and evidence. Progress to Early-Stage on either trigger: a share price at or below about SEK 85 (where the modal path returns about 20 percent a year over eighteen months), or a second acquisition of Vipa's scale announced at or below about 10x EBITA within twelve months of Vipa (which moves the cleared branch from about 40 percent toward probable and the fair multiple toward 15.5x). Drop the case on Q3 2026 (23-Oct-26) organic growth below 2 percent with a Rubber Compounding margin below 14 percent, or on no acquisition within twelve months of Vipa.
case: - The change is internal first, and it is funded rather than announced. A board that dismissed its chief executive in May 2026 for inaction installed a director from Atlas Copco on 1-Aug-26 with a mandate to deploy a balance sheet whose leverage ceiling it had raised from below 1.0x to 2.5x; the group was reorganised in January 2026 to report Thermoplastic Compounding separately; the first large deal of the new strategy, Vipa at EUR 143.5 million, was signed on 31-Jul-26 under the acting chief executive. Four of the twelve internal forces are strong (chief executive B; strategy B; acquisitions B; balance sheet B), meeting the framework's decision rule twice over, with no red flag present in full (permanent chief executive; leverage 1.15x against 2.5x; no debt-funded buyback). The "PowerPoint transformation" flag is partly live until Elmin's own deals appear. Headroom to the ceiling about SEK 4.5 billion (our estimate); DNB Carnegie models that deployment to 2.0x could add 33 to 52 percent to 2029 earnings.

- The external change is a turn in the company's own cycle, not a demand inflection. Twelve quarters of negative organic sales ended in Q2 2026 with +8 percent; the next two comparables are the weakest quarters in three years. Against it: order books "historically short and continue to become even shorter"; automotive flat in rubber; Americas +3 percent; DNB Carnegie says pre-buying ahead of mid-single-digit price rises may have supported Q2. The wire-and-cable niche growing 10 to 15 percent a year is about 12 percent of the business. External forces C: own cycle B; supply D; macroeconomic D; demand, competition, disruption, political each C.

- 'Financial Outputs' have turned up, one quarter deep. All four named brokers raised FY2026 and FY2027 EPS after Q2 (consensus FY2026 +7.6 percent, FY2027 +10.6 percent over three months); twelve-month revisions still negative. The outputs add up to about 8 percent EPS growth a year FY2025 to FY2028: revenue contributes about 6.7 percent a year (3 to 4 points organic, about 3 acquired), the margin nothing (company-basis EBITDA margin about 17.4 percent in FY2025 and about 17.4 percent in FY2028, because Rubber Compounding's operating-cost inflation and the lower-margin thermoplastics mix offset Mixing 5.0 and the thermoplastics margin recovery), below EBITDA about +1.9 percent a year, buybacks nothing with 0.27 percent LTIP dilution. The parts reconcile: 5.64 to about 7.25 on the company basis is ×1.285, 8.7 percent a year; 5.77 to 7.25 on the brokers' basis is 7.9 percent; consensus 5.77 to 7.30 is 8.2 percent. Cash conversion fell in Q2 2026 as safety stocks lifted net working capital to 15.3 percent of trailing sales.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, stated at its strongest: Q2 2026 was the profile the risks report calls a 'false friend', price rises and pre-buying masking flat volumes. Mid-single-digit price rises and customer pre-buying ahead of them, triggered by Middle East raw-material volatility, lifted organic sales 8 percent while underlying volumes stayed on the twelve-quarter trend; the risks report's own analysis of competing hypotheses found this profile had the fewest hard inconsistencies with the evidence. Rubber Compounding, 68 percent of sales, saw EBIT fall 5 percent and its margin fall 160 basis points in the same quarter. Automotive, 38 to 42 percent of volumes, was flat and faces European OEM profit warnings (Stellantis, Volkswagen) and a 2.6 percent cut to 2026 light-vehicle production; the Americas grew 3 percent. A destock follows in H2 2026 as raw materials stabilise. The new chief executive is a board insider hired within days of the dismissal, with no transaction record and no personal share purchase, at a company on its third chief executive in 36 months that loses two divisional presidents by end-2027; the acquisition pace has slowed since mid-2024 and the North American rubber pipeline is depleted and antitrust-limited. The krona is forecast to strengthen (Nordea: USD/SEK 9.23 at end-2027) and a 10 percent move takes about 9 percent off EBIT. The stock has re-rated 30 percent in three months to the 93rd percentile of its two-year range on one quarter; a trough multiple of 11.6x on SEK 7 of EPS is about SEK 82; the sell-side's bear case is 11x on about SEK 5, SEK 55 to 65. The risks report's pre-mortem puts the joint failure probability at 45 percent if a macro downturn overlaps a feedstock spike.

- Conceded: the pre-buy is plausible and unproven either way until 23-Oct-26; rubber's margin fell on operating costs, harder to price through than raw materials; the multiple is high against two years and the re-rating has happened before the evidence; Elmin is unproven and the bench is thinning; the krona is a real, unhedged drag on reported figures; the modal return at SEK 97 is a C. No segment covers the enterprise value: Rubber Compounding's run-rate adjusted EBIT of about SEK 2.2 billion after tax at 26.8 percent is about SEK 1.6 billion of post-tax earnings, about SEK 10 billion at the comparison set's lowest multiple (6.2x) and about SEK 22 billion at Hexpol's own 13.8x, 30 and 67 percent of the market capitalisation; the bounded-downside argument rests on the dividend, the balance sheet and the margin history, not on a sum of parts.
triggers: - Q3 2026 results on 23-Oct-26: organic growth below 2 percent with a Rubber Compounding margin below 14 percent moves the record to the pre-buy reading and drops the case; organic growth above 0 percent and a margin above 14 percent confirm; the one-month revision pace (+3 percent EPS; +0.7 percent FY2026) is already slowing, and the next print decides whether the three-month surge is a trend.

- Acquisition deployment: a second deal of Vipa's scale (about SEK 1.5 billion) at or below about 10x EBITA within twelve months of Vipa progresses the case; no acquisition within twelve months of Vipa is an Alarm and a drop; a deal above 12x EBITA is an Alarm (discipline fails); net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x without EPS accretion invalidates.

- Price: at or below about SEK 85 the modal path returns about 20 percent a year over eighteen months and the case progresses on the modal path alone (SEK 90 clears at eighteen months; SEK 80 at three years).

- Pass-through and margin: a sequential adjusted EBIT margin below 14 percent with pass-through cited as the cause invalidates (the sell-side's own invalidation line); a raw-material index spike above 10 percent in a quarter is an Alarm; Rubber Compounding's operating-cost inflation (−160 basis points in Q2 2026) is the forming risk.

- Demand: organic growth below 0 percent for two quarters (Alarm); S&P Global light-vehicle production growth below 0 percent (Alarm); European construction PMI below 45 (Alarm); the Americas (+3 percent in Q2 2026) and automotive (flat in rubber) are the soft spots; the Q2 2027 comparable against the +8 percent quarter is a hard step.

- Currency and raw materials: USD/SEK below 10.00 flags translation cuts (Alarm; Nordea forecasts 9.23 at end-2027); net working capital (15.3 percent of trailing sales at Q2 2026) should unwind as supply normalises; both are share-price risks, not case risks.
